html:
The Sultanate of Darfur was a state of the Fur people in what is now western Sudan, built around the volcanic Marrah Mountains. The map shows Darfur from 1530 to 1800.

Earlier kingdoms of the Daju and then the Tunjur ruled the region. In the 1600s the Keira dynasty of the Fur took power; Sulayman Solong, remembered as its founder, spread Islam at court. From the late 1700s the sultans ruled from a fixed capital at El Fasher.

Darfur grew rich on the Forty Days Road, the caravan route across the desert to Egypt, sending ivory, ostrich feathers, gum and enslaved people taken in raids to the south. It fought its western neighbour Wadai and the Funj sultanate to the east for control of Kordofan.

The sultanate fell to Egyptian forces in 1874, then came under the Mahdist state of the Mahdi. After the Mahdists were beaten, Sultan Ali Dinar restored it in about 1899, until British forces killed him and annexed Darfur to Sudan in 1916. Its people's later suffering is recorded in Darfur displacement.
